engagement_title: Vitale Labs, The Balance Brief three episode drop: cut three unedited lab takes into one series that sounds like one series, bring three mornings of on set stills to one cover look, and rebuild the printer's episode card into a live run
vertical: Health and wellness, direct to consumer supplements sold on subscription, short form educational video plus clinic partner and trade show print (Denver, Colorado)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com short form video post quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, seeking an editor for a health, wellness and genetics channel wanting 'educational, engaging, social-media driven' Reels and Shorts from a presenter who films long straight to camera takes, with the ideal freelancer explicitly comfortable with 'pacing, and social-media style'. The real company and presenter are laundered to the coined, IP clean brand Vitale Labs, its mini series The Balance Brief, and the presenter persona Dr. Nadia Reuter; no real brand, product, person or trademark is named. REPOSITIONED for connector reality, as the ledger's own note concedes: the literal post implies open timeline Premiere and After Effects work (multi track compositing, motion graphics, burned in captions, trim to timestamp assembly), none of which this connector performs. The honest fuller commission that same client genuinely needed is the whole drop rather than the timeline: automatic highlight cutting and same source reframing for the cuts, a speech pass judged across the set rather than per file, three mornings of on set stills brought to one cover look, the clinic partner episode card rebuilt from the press artwork as a real record per page run, and the on screen wording handed back as a working file the client edits when the air dates move. That is a posted job of the same shape and the same money, made producible.
client_one_liner: We have three episodes filmed and none of them cut, our cover stills were shot on three different mornings and do not look like one series, and the first one goes out in nine days.
client_brief:
Vitale Labs, The Balance Brief, first three episodes

We are a small direct to consumer supplement line in Denver. Our presenter, Dr. Nadia Reuter, films a short explainer series called The Balance Brief. Three episodes are shot and none of them are cut. They go out over a fortnight, one a week, and everything a viewer sees has to arrive together.

What we have. Each episode is one long take, straight to camera, one clip on mic, filmed in the same corner of our lab across three separate mornings. Nothing is trimmed, so there is chat at both ends. We also kept a second, higher resolution recording of each take for the vertical cuts.

What we need. A short landscape highlight per episode, around forty five seconds, for the site and the newsletter. A vertical cut per episode at full phone size for the feeds. Our regulatory reviewer cleared exactly one sentence per episode, and that sentence has to survive whole into every cut we publish. The sound has to be clean, and more than that, the three have to sound like the same series when somebody plays them one after another.

Every episode needs a cover picture. Our photographer shot stills alongside each morning. Side by side they do not look like one series yet, and one morning was shared with a supplier so there is other people's product on the bench.

For the trade show and our two clinic partners we reprint the episode card, one card per episode, from the artwork our printer used last season. The per episode details are in the sheet. Keep the card exactly as designed and change only what changes per episode.

Last, the caption and lower third sheet: the on screen wording for each episode, in a working file we can edit ourselves, because air dates move.

Our bottles are about forty dollars on subscription and our buyers are thirty to fifty, wellness curious and cautious about health claims. Credible and warm, never clinical, never hyped. Plus a note on what you did and anything we should know.
price_band_and_audience: A forty dollar monthly subscription supplement bought by a wellness curious thirty to fifty year old who has been burned by overclaiming. The band is load bearing in both directions. Push it up into near black grounds, cold hard light, a slow authored title sequence and a whispered voice and it becomes a two hundred dollar longevity clinic, which misprices a forty dollar bottle and reads as a claim the reviewer never cleared. Push it down into saturated fast cuts, shouted supers, a bright bounce grade and stacked benefit captions and it becomes a discount aisle stack of gummies, which in this category reads as hype and is precisely what makes a cautious buyer close the tab. The correct answer sits between them: daylight in a real lab, unhurried pacing, a warm neutral rather than a clinical blue, restrained type, and one cleared sentence given room rather than six claims crammed in. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even where every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,400 to 3,000 dollars fixed for the drop.

brand_identity.sector: Direct to consumer supplement line sold on subscription, with a short form educational video series.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2018, Denver, Colorado, a small direct to consumer supplement company with an in house presenter.
brand_identity.about: Vitale Labs is a small Denver supplement line sold direct to consumers on subscription. Its presenter, Dr. Nadia Reuter, fronts a short explainer series, The Balance Brief, that turns one cleared claim per episode into a calm, credible watch. The brand's whole positioning is restraint: it speaks to buyers who have been burned by overclaiming, and it rewards being believed over being loud.
brand_identity.audience: Wellness curious buyers aged 30 to 50, cautious about health claims and burned by overclaiming before. They reward evidence and plain speech, and they close the tab on hype.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Bottles around 40 dollars a month on subscription. Positioned between a discount gummy stack and a 200 dollar longevity clinic: credible and warm, never clinical and never hyped.
brand_identity.typography: Display: a warm, humanist serif that reads as considered rather than clinical. Text: a clean humanist sans, generous and unhurried. One cleared sentence is given room rather than six claims crammed in. Nothing cold and nothing shouted.
brand_identity.voice: Measured, warm and plain. States what is known and stops there. Example line: 'One change, explained clearly. No promises we cannot keep.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The brand runs on the artwork its printer used last season. The episode card exists as the press PDF the printer worked from, and the per episode details live in a supplied sheet. Type and colour direction are inherited from that card rather than from a formal guideline, and the regulatory reviewer's cleared claim lines are fixed and cannot be reworded.
brand_identity.values: Credibility over reach: never a claim the reviewer did not clear.

assets_supplied.name: balance_brief_takes/ (3 landscape takes, one per episode, untrimmed)
assets_supplied.kind: Single camera straight to camera takes filmed on three separate mornings in the same corner of the lab, one clip on microphone per take, nothing trimmed at either end.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "One long take per episode, same corner, same setup. There is chat before and after because nobody stopped recording."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The takes do not behave alike under an automatic highlight cut. In episode two the presenter turns to the bench mid take and the clip mic goes off axis for a long stretch that still looks composed on screen, and in episode three the cleared sentence sits near the very end, after the natural energy peak, so a cut drawn to the liveliest material returns a plausible, well paced highlight with the one sentence that must survive missing entirely and the off axis stretch left in, at full success.

assets_supplied.name: balance_brief_masters/ (3 higher resolution recordings of the same three takes)
assets_supplied.kind: The second, higher resolution recording of each take, kept for the vertical cuts.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The bigger files, same performances, for the phone cuts."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Only two of the three are what the folder implies. The episode two file came off a different body that morning and its frame is materially shorter than its neighbours, which no filename, folder or note reveals, so the vertical cut for that episode cannot reach full phone size from its own source and the resize tool will not enlarge it to get there.

assets_supplied.name: balance_brief_stills/ (9 on set stills, 3 per morning, camera scale)
assets_supplied.kind: Stills the photographer shot alongside each filming morning, three per episode, natural window light on two mornings and a panel on the third.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The covers come from these. Three per morning. Put them together and they do not look like one series yet, and one morning we shared the bench with a supplier."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The panel lit morning renders the presenter's white lab coat with a cast that a single warm correction across the set turns green rather than neutral, so that morning needs a confined correction the other two do not. Separately the only frame from that morning with usable expression carries a supplier's carton at the right edge, which cannot be retouched out and can only be cropped away, and cropping far enough to lose it takes the frame under the cover size the feeds need, with enlargement the only way back.

assets_supplied.name: balance_card_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The press PDF the printer used for last season's episode card, one card, a continuous block of set copy over a portrait frame.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card exactly as it went to press last season. Please keep the design and change only the per episode details."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Its typeset copy is one continuous flow, so it converts to a single text frame rather than the separate title, presenter and detail frames the printed page suggests, and the mapping readout for that frame silently omits one run while keeping its line break, so every offset computed past that point is short by exactly that run and the validator still returns valid. The title measure is also fixed and does not spill: a record longer than last season's simply stops rendering at trim.

assets_supplied.name: balance_episodes.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Three rows, one per episode: episode title, presenter name, air date, the cleared claim line, the short link and the per episode portrait filename.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The three episodes as they will run. The claim lines are the ones our reviewer signed off and cannot be reworded."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The third episode's title runs to nearly twice the character count of the other two, which nothing in the sheet flags and which only matters once it is set into the card's fixed title measure at trim.

assets_supplied.name: balance_captions.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The on screen wording per episode: opening lower third, presenter credit, the cleared sentence as it must appear, and the closing card wording.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The words that go on screen. The cleared sentence has to appear exactly as written."

acceptance_bar: Each landscape highlight lands near the runtime asked and contains, whole and audible, the one sentence the reviewer cleared for that episode. A well paced cut without that sentence is not a deliverable.
No cut shows the presenter off microphone or off frame, and nothing from before or after the take survives into any published cut.
No delivered video exceeds its own source frame, and a vertical cut that cannot reach full phone size from its own source is named in the note rather than enlarged to reach it.

Played back to back the three episodes sound like one series: one voice character, one level, one room. An episode that is clean on its own but sits brighter or quieter than its neighbours fails, because the three are heard as a set and never alone.

The three covers read as one series at feed size: one white point, one warmth, one crop logic, the presenter at one height in frame. A morning that cannot be brought to the set is named, not shipped at eighty percent.
No cover carries another company's packaging, and no cover reaches its size by being enlarged. Both at once, on the same frame, is the actual requirement.

The printed card is unchanged in design and only the per episode details differ, and every one of those details renders whole at trim. A record whose title stops short of its last word fails even where every file reports success.
The card run is one press file carrying one page per episode in the order of the sheet, plus a proof per episode at print resolution for the clinic partners to sign off.

The caption and lower third sheet is one working file the client can edit, every canvas keeping its own size, the wording live text rather than a picture of wording, and every caption legible over the frame it actually sits on rather than over white.
One type system across the card and the sheet, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.
The note states, per episode, what was applied to picture and to sound and why that episode differs from its neighbours, every resize any tool reported, and anything that could not be delivered.

adobe_surfaces.role: One type system carrying both the printed card and the on screen wording. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land credible and warm rather than clinical or hyped. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical form before the kit call because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or it falls back with no warning.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a frame.
trajectory.judgement: Three destinations with three different natures: cuts that can only be shortened, a printed card whose design is frozen and needs a record per page, and on screen wording the client edits later, which only an authored fixed canvas document gives back. The brief pins all three, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming the surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handover discipline: a manifest keyed by role, so that forty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which episode.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by episode and role.

trajectory.action: Read each untrimmed take end to end: where the cleared sentence sits inside it, where the take genuinely comes alive, and where it is unusable.
trajectory.judgement: The client believes three takes are three equivalent performances. They are three different mornings and the one sentence that must survive does not sit in the same place in each. Locating it is the only thing that makes the later cut judgeable.
trajectory.produces: A per take reading noting the position of the cleared sentence, the shape of the take, and any stretch that must not reach a published cut.

trajectory.action: Run the speech pass on each take, choosing per take rather than applying one setting to all three.
trajectory.judgement: Three mornings and one microphone placement that was not identical. The pass is a judgement about each recording, not a switch, and the client's real requirement is a set that sounds like one series rather than three individually clean files.
trajectory.produces: Three passed audio takes with the setting used on each recorded.

trajectory.action: Cut the landscape highlight for each episode toward the runtime the client asked for, then watch each result all the way through rather than reading the response.
trajectory.judgement: The only levers are the source given and the runtime asked; nothing selects which moments are kept. Watching the whole cut, not sampling it, is the only way the cleared sentence and the off axis stretch can be accounted for.
trajectory.produces: Three landscape highlights, each watched end to end, with what each cut actually contains written down.

trajectory.action: Bring each vertical cut to full phone size from that episode's higher resolution recording, reading the dimensions that came back against the ones asked for, then play the three finished episodes back to back.
trajectory.judgement: The tool will not enlarge, so a shortfall is a fact about the source rather than a parameter to raise. Playing the three adjacent is the only place the client's actual requirement, that they sound like one series, can be tested at all.
trajectory.produces: Three vertical cuts with their returned dimensions recorded, and a set level listening note across the three.

trajectory.action: Preview all nine stills and triage them: which morning each belongs to, its illuminant, its tilt, what sits at the edges of frame, and which frame per episode carries the usable expression.
trajectory.judgement: Three per morning is not three interchangeable frames. The cover is chosen on expression first, and the constraints of the chosen frame then set the whole crop plan for that episode.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering morning, illuminant, tilt, edge content and expression.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the subject and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop that was chosen against the unstraightened frame.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one credible warm target off the best lit morning and correct each still toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a series, not nine good photographs. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for frames shot under two different light sources; the destination is single and the routes are not.
trajectory.produces: Nine graded masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Confine the correction where a whole frame move goes wrong, selecting the material by its own visual properties rather than by the object it belongs to.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the entire gate: naming the garment's owner pulls the selection to the person, naming the fabric's own appearance pulls it to the fabric. Only the panel lit morning needs this.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a global move would have taken the coat green or the bench muddy.

trajectory.action: Cut the three covers at feed size and produce the per episode portrait the printed card will bind, reading every returned tradeoff record rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: On the shared bench frame the crop that loses the supplier's carton and the crop that holds the cover size pull against each other, and the tradeoffs object is the only channel that reports what the tool did to the dimensions. Two different destinations, two different crop logics, one grade.
trajectory.produces: Three covers at feed size, three card portraits on the house ground, and every returned tradeoff recorded.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a forty dollar subscription and a claim wary reader: credible and warm, not clinical and not hyped. The weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's press PDF, export the interchange file, and read the document's real frame inventory rather than the printed page's apparent structure.
trajectory.judgement: What the converted document exposes as separate frames is not under anyone's control and often does not match what the printed card looks like. Promising a field to a frame before looking is a guess.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory with counts, bounds, applied type and existing links.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct each frame's true story text from the interchange file itself, compute every offset from that string, build the mapping, validate it, prepare the merge template and re export to confirm every placeholder actually landed.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping readout is a convenience, not the document. A validator that reports valid and a preparation step that reports success are both compatible with fields silently absent, so the only honest confirmation is finding each placeholder in the round tripped file.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose every field is confirmed present by inspection rather than by a success message.

trajectory.action: Merge the three rows to one press file and render a per episode proof at print resolution, then look at each page at trim.
trajectory.judgement: Page count matching row count is necessary and nowhere near sufficient. The client's requirement is that the details render, and only a page viewed at trim shows whether they did.
trajectory.produces: One press file of three pages in sheet order, three print resolution proofs, and a per page reading at trim.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying a root per format the client posts to, inline every frame behind a caption as image data, set the caption blocks on a legibility ground, declare family and weight on every text element, let each root declare its own canvas, then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A frame left as a reference is not a frame, a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set, and the design work is how much room the cleared sentence gets against a face. Caption legibility over a real frame is the client's actual requirement, so the ground behind the words is a design decision rather than decoration.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the whole caption and lower third sheet, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per canvas markup for every other canvas.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning of any kind, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at canvas one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Write the note: per episode picture and sound decisions, the set level listening judgement, every resize any tool reported, the type system by role, and anything that could not be delivered.
trajectory.judgement: The client is buying a series they will extend themselves. A note that repeats the deliverable list is worthless; one that names what the next episode's footage must avoid is the actual value.
trajectory.produces: A written handover note against the run, naming limitations explicitly.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the automatic highlight cut actually kept out of each untrimmed take. The cutting tool shortens only, chooses its own moments, and exposes no control over which ones: the only levers are the source it is handed and the runtime it is asked for. On episode three the cleared sentence sits after the natural energy peak, so a cut drawn to the liveliest material comes back well paced, correctly timed and entirely plausible with that sentence absent; on episode two the stretch where the presenter turns off axis still looks composed on screen and survives into the cut. Both results report full success, and which take behaves which way is a property of that morning's performance, not of the request.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because the selection happens inside the tool and there is no read ahead of what it will keep. The brief states that the cleared sentence must survive, which is the client's standing requirement, but nothing anywhere states that an automatic cut will drop it, and a competent agent has every reason to expect a highlight of a straight to camera explainer to include its punchline. The response is not the same call again: it is a different route per episode, feeding the paired recording whose different material yields a different selection, or asking for a longer runtime and then judging whether the highlight still reads at that length, or concluding that this episode cannot be cut automatically to the runtime asked and delivering it longer with the reason named.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the cut route per episode rather than per batch, re-cut from the alternate source or at a revised runtime, watch every result end to end again rather than sampling it, and carry any runtime the client did not ask for into the handover note with the reason.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A supplement brand publishes three health explainers in which the only sentences its regulatory reviewer cleared do not appear, and one in which the presenter goes off microphone on camera, on a series whose entire proposition is that it is credible.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the three finished episodes sound like one series when they are played one after another. The speech pass reports success on each file, each file sounds clean on its own, and nothing in the family returns a loudness, tonal or room readout of any kind. Episode two's microphone sat differently that morning, so the same pass that rescues it also thins it, and the divergence is a property of the set rather than of any file: it is inaudible on any single playback and obvious the moment the three run back to back in a feed, which is how the client's audience will meet them.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: There is no ordering that surfaces it earlier, because the comparison only exists once all three cuts exist, and there is no measurement to consult in place of listening. The brief asks for clean sound and for the three to sound like one series, which is the client's goal, but nothing states that the pass will pull one episode away from its neighbours, and applying the identical pass to three files is the reasonable first move rather than a mistake. The response is a different decision rather than a repeat: which episode is the reference for the set, whether episode two takes the pass at all, and whether the pass belongs on the source take ahead of the cut rather than after it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-decide the reference episode, re-run or withhold the pass on the divergent take, re-cut anything whose audio was passed after cutting rather than before, and re-listen to all three adjacent rather than checking the one that changed.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A fortnightly series in which the middle episode is audibly a different recording setup from the two around it, which reads to a claim wary audience as three unrelated videos rather than one series, and which the client will only hear after publishing.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether every per episode value actually renders on the page it belongs to. The card's title measure is fixed and does not spill: it simply stops rendering, so a record longer than last season's is silently truncated at trim with no overset flag anywhere in the chain. Upstream, the mapping readout for the card's single collapsed text frame omits one run while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well formed and every offset computed past it is short by exactly that run, and the validator returns valid on those offsets while the preparation step reports completed successfully. The merge then returns one file whose page count matches the row count exactly. Only a page viewed at trim shows a title stopping short of its last word and a field that never landed.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Nothing in the ordering exposes it, because every response in the chain is a success and the one honest signal, the rendered page at trim, exists only at the end. The brief supplies the sheet and asks that the card design be kept and only the per episode details change, which is the client's constraint rather than a disclosure that one title outruns its frame or that a readout drops a run. The response is a different mapping decision rather than another merge: recompute the offsets from the document's own reconstructed story text, re-plan which value carries in which frame given the true frame granularity, and take a wording decision back to the client where the copy genuinely cannot fit a frozen measure.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the mapping from the reconstructed story text, re-prepare the template and confirm each placeholder by inspection, agree an abbreviated title with the client where the measure cannot hold the full one, then re-merge and re-read every page at trim rather than trusting the page count.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Three hundred cards go to a trade show and two clinic partners with one episode's title cut off mid word and a field missing on every card, from a run that reported valid, successful and correctly paginated at every step.

deliverables.name: The Balance Brief cut set, landscape highlights and vertical cuts
deliverables.spec: Three landscape highlights near the runtime asked, each containing the cleared sentence whole and audible and nothing from before or after the take, plus three vertical cuts at full phone size where the source allows it. No output exceeds its own source frame, and any cut that could not reach the size or the runtime asked is named with the reason rather than enlarged or padded. This is one series of six files, not one file at six sizes.

deliverables.name: The Balance Brief cover set and card portraits
deliverables.spec: Three episode covers at feed size brought to one series look, one white point, one warmth, one crop logic and the presenter at one height in frame across three different filming mornings, with a confined correction where a global move fails, plus the per episode portrait variant on the house ground that the printed card binds. No cover carries another company's packaging and no cover reaches its size by enlargement. Per frame parameter log included, with one line on why each morning differs from its neighbours.

deliverables.name: Episode card run for the clinic partners and the trade show
deliverables.spec: The printer's press artwork rebuilt into a live run: one press file carrying one page per episode in sheet order, with the per episode portrait genuinely bound per record rather than one static picture repeated, plus a print resolution proof per episode for partner sign off. The card design is unchanged, and every per episode value renders whole at trim, confirmed by reading each page rather than by the page count.

deliverables.name: Caption and lower third sheet, as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable document carrying a root per format the client posts to, each keeping its own canvas size, with the on screen wording as live text in one licensed type system, every frame behind a caption carried as embedded image data rather than a reference, and every caption legible over the frame it actually sits on. Delivered with the self contained source it was authored from, which is the durable half: the client edits the document when air dates move, and the source guarantees the design survives regardless.

deliverables.name: Series handover note
deliverables.spec: A written note recording per episode what was applied to picture and to sound and why that episode differs from its neighbours, the set level listening judgement and which episode is the reference, every resize any tool reported with the file it applied to, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and actual numeric weight, any wording change agreed with the client and why, and what the next filming morning must do differently for the fourth episode to cut cleanly.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are cuts that can only be shortened, which need a record per page run, and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free form layout.
Which source each highlight is cut from, and whether the runtime the client asked for is compatible with the sentence that must survive in that particular take.
Whether an episode that cannot be cut automatically to the runtime asked is delivered longer, delivered shorter, or named as not deliverable that way at all.
Whether the speech pass is one setting across three mornings or a per take judgement, and which episode is the reference the other two are brought to.
Where the vertical cut's size ceiling actually comes from, and how to say that one episode cannot reach full phone size without pretending it can.
How far the panel lit morning can be brought toward the other two before it stops being worth saving, versus naming it.
On the shared bench frame, how to reconcile losing the supplier's carton with holding the cover size, when only one of those is free.
Selection wording for the confined correction: naming the person pulls the selection to the person, naming the fabric's own appearance pulls it to the fabric.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a claim wary buyer at a forty dollar band, plus the real numeric weight per family.
Which values can be bound to which frames once the converted card's true frame granularity is known, rather than which the printed page appears to offer.
What to do when a cleared, unrewordable line meets a frozen measure: take a wording decision back to the client, or move the value to a frame that can carry it.
How much room the cleared sentence gets against a face on the caption canvases. At this band restraint is the design, and a dense benefit stack is a correct looking wrong answer.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image or video model and it returns a plausible wellness explainer with a presenter who is not Dr. Nadia Reuter saying sentences no regulatory reviewer cleared. IDENTITY: these are this brand's actual three takes, this presenter's actual performances, this photographer's actual mornings, and this printer's actual card artwork, and the one sentence per episode that must survive is a compliance artefact rather than a line to be paraphrased. SPEC: the client needs one press file carrying one page per episode in sheet order at print resolution with per record portraits genuinely bound, plus cuts at exact phone size that were never enlarged, none of which a generated asset satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the caption sheet is defined by being editable, since the air dates move and the client explicitly cannot re commission. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality that no generation performs: did this cut actually keep the cleared sentence, do these three sound like one series when played adjacent, did this title render to its last word at trim.
doability_proof: Every link sits inside the verified permitted set, five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability. VIDEO AND AUDIO is confined to the four permitted operations only: media_summarize to read the takes, media_enhance_speech for the speech pass, video_create_quick_cut which shortens only and is never asked to lengthen, and video_resize which never enlarges and is never asked to. No deliverable depends on frame extraction, trim to timestamp assembly, multi track compositing, motion graphics, burned in captions or format conversion, which is exactly why the on screen wording is a separate authored document rather than a burn in. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, auto_tone, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence and upscale_factor, and remove_background in its backgroundColor form are all verified headless. The no enlargement gate is checkable against the returned upscale factor and tradeoffs rather than asserted, and the substrate versus material prompt asymmetry is a live finding that makes the confined correction a real decision. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt as both mapper and validator, prepare_indd_merge_template and document_merge_data_layout are verified end to end from a bare press PDF, with one record per page confirmed for PDF output, an at prefixed image column plus additionalImageFiles confirmed to bind per row images, and per record proofs produced by rendering separately because merge output ignores its own resolution field. The card checkpoint rests on three documented findings: the mapping readout is lossy and shifts every offset past the omission while the validator still reports valid, frame granularity from a PDF is not under the author's control, and success messages are compatible with silently dropped mappings. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, the product is a genuine editable document findable by asset_search, photographs must be embedded as image data because references render as empty grey boxes at full success, and the rendition preview is documented as first canvas only, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined stills pass the inline threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end, with the case sensitivity and non standard numeric weight traps live. AVOIDED: no text to image, no generative fill or expand, no object removal, no compositing, no upscaling, no OCR, no vector render or vector merge, no fill_text, no animate_design, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above twenty files.
